THOUGHT: The clinical lesion is a slowly growing, 1.2-cm brown mammillated plaque on the scalp with protruding terminal hairs. Dermoscopy showed brown (pigment) globules, milialike cysts, and focal arborizing vessels — features that can mimic pigmented basal cell carcinoma or a pigmented adnexal/pilar lesion. The histopathology is the key: epidermal projections of monotonous basaloid and squamous epithelial cells, presence of poroid (poroid-type) cells and cystic structures, well-formed ductal structures with an eosinophilic cuticle, and islands containing mature sebocytes. Those features point to an adnexal (poroid) neoplasm showing ductal (eccrine/poroid) differentiation with focal sebaceous differentiation. This pattern is most consistent with a poroid neoplasm (eccrine poroma/hidroacanthoma simplex/poroid hidradenoma spectrum) with sebaceous differentiation (a reported benign variant). Other entities that can present similarly clinically or histologically include sebaceoma/adenoma (because of mature sebocytes), pigmented basal cell carcinoma (arborizing vessels, basaloid islands, pigment), follicular/basaloid tumors such as trichoblastoma or trichoepithelioma, and organoid/nevus sebaceus on the scalp. The histologic presence of poroid cells and ductal cuticle strongly favors a poroid (poroma/poroid neoplasm) as the most likely diagnosis.

DIAGNOSIS:
1. Poroid adnexal neoplasm (eccrine poroma / hidroacanthoma simplex / poroid hidradenoma spectrum) with sebaceous differentiation — most likely
2. Sebaceoma (benign sebaceous tumor) / sebaceous adenoma — possible given mature sebocytes, but less favored because of prominent poroid/ductal structures
3. Pigmented basal cell carcinoma — considered because of basaloid islands, pigment globules, and arborizing vessels on dermoscopy, but histologic ductal/poroid and sebaceous differentiation argue against BCC
4. Trichoblastoma / trichoepithelioma (benign follicular basaloid tumor) — can mimic clinically and histologically (basaloid proliferation) but lacks the clear poroid ductal structures and sebaceous differentiation seen here
5. Nevus sebaceus (organoid sebaceous nevus) or other organoid epidermal nevus with adnexal differentiation — scalp location and sebaceous elements fit, but the adult-onset, solitary small lesion and poroid histology make this less likely
